sources.title: 2026 Minnesota Income Tax Withholding Instruction Booklet and Tax Tables

steps: Multiply wages for the payroll period by the applicable number of payroll periods.
Subtract $5,300 for each W-4MN allowance; if the result is zero or less, withholding is zero before requested additional withholding.
Apply the annual filing-status schedule to the remaining annualized wages.
Divide annual tax by payroll periods and add requested additional periodic withholding. The employer may round withholding to the nearest dollar.

supplementalWages.separatelyRecordedAlternative: Aggregate the regular and supplemental wages and subtract tax already withheld from regular wages.
supplementalWages.notSeparatelyRecorded: Aggregation with regular wages is mandatory.

residencyAndWorkRules.residentRule: Minnesota residents are subject to Minnesota withholding on wages for services inside and outside Minnesota, subject to the actual other-state-withholding credit method.
residencyAndWorkRules.residentWorkingOutsideMinnesota: Compute Minnesota withholding and subtract tax actually withheld by the other state for the same wages, but never reduce Minnesota withholding below zero.
residencyAndWorkRules.nonresidentRule: Withhold only from wages for services performed in Minnesota unless an exception applies.

nonresidentAnnualPayThreshold.effect: No Minnesota withholding when expected annual Minnesota wages are below the threshold.

residencyAndWorkRules.reciprocityRenewal: Annual; employer sends the form to Minnesota Revenue.
residencyAndWorkRules.interstateRailAndMotorCarrierRule: Withhold only for the employee's state of residence.
residencyAndWorkRules.airCarrierRule: Withholding jurisdiction is the state of residence and any state in which more than 50% of scheduled flight time is worked.

depositSchedules.due: Wednesday for Wednesday-Friday paydays; Friday for Saturday-Tuesday paydays

conditions: Prior-quarter Minnesota withholding was $1,500 or less
Previous return was filed on time
Previous annual withholding was $500 or less
depositSchedules.due: January 31; if cumulative withholding exceeds $500 during the year, deposit by the last day of the following month except December

electronicPaymentTriggers: Withholding and other specified Minnesota taxes totaled at least $10,000 during the 12 months ending June 30
Required to pay another Minnesota business tax electronically
Payment made by a payroll service
filing.returns: Generally quarterly through e-Services; zero returns remain required while the account is open.

captureWarnings: The complete wage-bracket matrices remain in the checksummed official booklet and are not transcribed into this capture.
The resident other-state credit requires actual other-state withholding and pay-period state, not merely a nominal other-state rate.
Nonresident entertainer withholding is a separate tax workflow and must not be treated as ordinary employee wage withholding.
